messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PROD alert — GPU pool `gpool-nyc-1` saturated, queue depth spike > 1200, p95 latency increasing. Paging on-call.
ash: on it. seeing user-facing errors in traces? any customer impact reported?
samir: looking. APM shows tail errors from our generation endpoints (api-v2) starting 14:23:10 UTC. Error type: 504 gateway + backend timeout. customer-facing rate ~0.8% of requests/min at peak.
maya: runtime metrics: all GPUs in gpool-nyc-1 at 100% memory/util. kv-cache miss rate jumped to 93% at 14:22. prefix-cache cold start storm.
ash: hypothesis: cold cache + HPA slow reaction -> requests backlogged in the queue while new pods warm up (model weights pulling + quant init).
eli: sharing kube/HPA logs now — HPA events show scale-up triggered at 14:22:35 but controller reported CPU metrics lag and only added 1 replica by 14:26:00. expected ~6.
samir: paste: ```
Events:
  14:22:35  HorizontalPodAutoscaler scaled up from 3 to 4 replicas (metrics below threshold)
  14:25:58  HorizontalPodAutoscaler scaled up from 4 to 5 replicas
  14:29:12  HorizontalPodAutoscaler scaled up from 5 to 7 replicas
``` 
maya: warmup histogram: new-pod-ready-to-serving median 180s, 95th 320s. our warmup work (weights + quant) is dominating.
ash: immediate mitigation options: 1) manual surge (increase desired replicas in gpool) 2) route traffic to secondary region (latency/cost) 3) temporarily enable fallback smaller model for non-critical customers.
ops-bot: runbook link — https://internal/runbooks/autoscale-coldstart
eli: I manually bumped Deployment desiredReplicas to 10 for gpool-nyc-1 (kubectl scale --replicas=10). watching.
ash: good. also starting parallel: prepull images and run quick warmup init on 3 spare nodes (maya, can you run warmup script?)
maya: running warmup script on new pods: ```
for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l app=gpool-nyc-1 -o name); do
  kubectl exec $pod -- /opt/runtime/bin/warmup --model-id redwood-v1 --prefix-cache
done
``` 
ash: timeline notes: 14:22 alert fired -> 14:22 scale trigger -> 14:26 first extra replica -> 14:35 manual scale to 10 -> 14:40 warmups finishing -> 14:44 latency returning to normal.
samir: logs attached (snippet): "queue_depth=1283, pending_reqs=1240, hpa_replicas=3, gpu_util=0.98" at 14:23:45. forwarding to postmortem doc.
eli: customer impact calc: peak 0.8% error rate across requests; affected set includes a small subset of enterprise customers (3 tenants) with strict SLAs. Notified CS.
ash: actions assigned: samir -> gather HPA controller metrics and kube-controller manager logs; maya -> warmup optimization plan + quant init profiling; eli -> customer impact thread + CS handoff; ash -> write initial RCA timeline (in this thread) and link to incident channel.
ops-bot: pager cleared? :white_check_mark:
ash: marking page resolved for now. follow-up: create RCA with root cause: autoscaler inertia + cold cache storm + slow warmup sequence. hypothesis to validate: (A) HPA metric selection (CPU) not reflecting real GPU/model warmup cost; (B) caching strategy allowed cache-thrash on deployment churn.
samir: grabbing controller logs and will post PR with metric adapter to expose GPU memory pressure to HPA.
maya: will instrument warmup bootstrap to parallelize weight load + quant steps to cut median warmup to <60s.
eli: I opened incident-306678-rca draft and added customer impact section. linking once you all approve.
ash: nice triage. closing live thread — leave follow-up comments in incident-306678-rca. Thanks all :thumbsup:
